title: Anomalous Hall and Nernst effects driven by static and fluctuating spin chiralities on Kagome lattice
authors: He-Lin Li, Zhen-Gang Zhu, Gang Su
abstract: We theoretically investigate the anomalous Hall and Nernst effects (AHE and ANE) in a two dimensional Kagome lattice to uncover the distinct roles of static and fluctuating scalar spin chi ralities. Employing Monte Carlo simulations incorporating with a tight binding Hamiltonian via the s-d exchange interaction, we explicitly evaluate the anomalous transport coefficients. A key finding is the systematic disentanglement of the macroscopic responses into an intrinsic contribu tion, governed by momentum space Berry curvature induced by static chirality, and an extrinsic skew scattering contribution driven by real space dynamical spin fluctuations. We demonstrate a pronounced mechanistic crossover: deep in magnetically ordered phases like the skyrmion crystal, the intrinsic Berry curvature dictates the transport behavior. However, approaching the magnetic order-disorder critical regime, strong thermal fluctuations disrupt static noncoplanar spin configu rations, drastically suppressing intrinsic responses. Here, dynamical chiral fluctuations emerge as the dominant driving force. By delineating the phase regimes governed by static versus fluctuating chiralities, this work elucidates the distinct microscopic mechanisms dictating anomalous transport in frustrated magnetic systems.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes anomalous Hall and Nernst effects in a Kagome lattice by separating their origins into contributions from static spin chirality (intrinsic) and dynamic spin fluctuations (extrinsic). The key finding is the identification of a phase crossover where thermal fluctuations suppress topological responses, allowing dynamical chiral fluctuations to dominate transport behavior.
main_problem: The study investigates the distinct roles of static versus fluctuating spin chiralities in driving anomalous Hall and Nernst effects in a frustrated magnetic lattice.
main_result: A pronounced mechanistic crossover is demonstrated: intrinsic transport is governed by Berry curvature in ordered phases, while dynamic fluctuations dominate near the order-disorder critical regime.
method: The authors combine Monte Carlo simulations with semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory to calculate anomalous scattering rates using perturbation expansions up to the second Born approximation.
model_or_system: The system is a two-dimensional Kagome lattice hosting itinerant electrons coupled to localized magnetic moments via an s-d exchange interaction. The analysis uses a Kondo-type Hamiltonian framework.
key_observables: Anomalous Hall Conductivity (AHC, $\sigma_{xy}$) and Anomalous Nernst Effect ($\alpha_{xy}$), decomposed into intrinsic (Berry curvature) and extrinsic (skew scattering) contributions.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), chemical potential ($\epsilon$), magnetic order parameters, and the strength of the exchange coupling ($J_K$).
main_assumptions: The analysis employs a low-energy effective mass approximation for band dispersion and utilizes the relaxation time approximation within the Boltzmann equation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing topological quantities ($\chi_{total}$, $\chi_Q$, etc.) across T-B parameter space, and show real-space spin configurations corresponding to different magnetic phases (e.g., skyrmion crystal).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by deriving the general expressions for anomalous transport coefficients using scattering theory, then applying these formalisms to the Kagome lattice to explicitly separate and analyze the contributions from static vs. dynamic chiralities across various magnetic phase regimes.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the rigorous separation of intrinsic (topological/Berry curvature) versus extrinsic (scattering-rate dependent) responses mirrors general principles used in analyzing non-equilibrium transport in complex quantum systems.
